after: ## Where this fits in the subject
alt: Discrete: biology, chemistry and physics run side by side all year as separate subjects. Modular: the sciences are taught one after another in rotation across the year. Integrated: the disciplines are blended into one course.
caption: The same sciences can be packaged as discrete, modular or integrated courses.

after: ## eAssessment scope is set by the option, not the course model
alt: The course model (discrete, modular or integrated) does not set the examination scope. The eAssessment option (biology, chemistry, physics or integrated sciences) sets which topics the examination draws on, from a list spanning atomic structure and bonding, cells, cycles, electromagnetism, evolution, interactions between organisms, forces, states and properties of matter, metabolism, organisms and waves.
caption: Your eAssessment option, not your school’s course model, sets what the exam can examine.

after: ## Worked example: organising revision across a modular timetable
alt: A modular year taught biology in term 1, chemistry in term 2 and physics in term 3. Revising only physics is risky because the exam can draw on any content in the option’s scope. The better plan keeps one summary sheet per module and reviews them in rotation before the exam.
caption: Revisit every module in your option’s scope, not just the most recent one.

alt: A bar of 100 marks split in half: the investigation-skills task, criteria B and C, carries 50 marks and the other tasks the remaining 50. Revision time should match, with practice at hypotheses and interpreting imperfect data, not only recall.
caption: Investigation skills carry half the marks, so they deserve half the revision time.

after: ## Key and related concepts still apply across all models
alt: Discrete, modular and integrated courses all feed into the same framework: the key concepts change, relationships and systems; related concepts such as energy, movement, transformation and models; the six global contexts; and one investigation-skills task.
caption: Whatever the course model, the concepts and the skills task are the same.

alt: Three steps: confirm your course model and your eAssessment option; schedule revision that revisits every module in the option’s scope; and give investigation skills about half the time, matching their 50% share of marks.
caption: Confirm model and option, cover every module, and weight the skills task.
